subject: Art and Culture
sub_topic: Stupa — origin, components (anda, harmika, chattra, torana)

concepts.name: Stupa: Etymology and Original Purpose
key_dimensions: Pre-Buddhist origins as burial mounds vs Buddhist adaptation
Evolution from relic repository to commemorative monument
Distinction between dhatu (relic) stupas and paribhogika (objects used by Buddha) stupas
Symbolic transformation from funerary to worship architecture

concepts.name: Anda (Hemispherical Dome): Symbolism and Evolution
key_dimensions: Representation of cosmic egg/universe (Brahmanda)
Proportional changes from early (Sanchi) to later periods (Amaravati)
Solid vs hollow anda construction techniques
Regional variations: cylindrical (Gandhara) vs hemispherical (Indian mainland)

concepts.name: Harmika: Structure and Significance
key_dimensions: Square railing on top of anda representing abode of gods
Distinction between harmika and medhi (terrace)
Presence/absence in different stupa traditions (prominent in Sanchi, minimal in Amaravati)
Connection to Vedic fire altar symbolism

concepts.name: Chattra (Umbrella): Hierarchical Symbolism
key_dimensions: Number of chhatras indicating spiritual hierarchy (single vs triple)
Evolution from single parasol to multi-tiered yasti (axial pole)
Royal insignia symbolism vs cosmic axis (axis mundi) interpretation
Differences between Indian stupas (3 chhatras) and East Asian pagodas (multiple tiers)

concepts.name: Torana (Gateway): Architectural and Narrative Function
key_dimensions: Four cardinal directions and their specific iconographic themes
Structural elements: posts (stambha), architraves, and bracket figures (salabhanjika)
Absence of Buddha images vs symbolic representations (Bodhi tree, footprints, wheel)
Comparison: Sanchi toranas (narrative richness) vs Bharhut (simpler design)

concepts.name: Vedika (Railing): Types and Ritual Significance
key_dimensions: Double vedika system: inner (around anda) and outer (ground level)
Material evolution: wooden prototypes to stone replicas
Pradakshina path (circumambulation) facilitation
Decorative motifs: lotus medallions, yaksha figures, and their meanings

concepts.name: Medhi (Circular Terrace): Functional and Symbolic Aspects
key_dimensions: Elevated pradakshina path for devotees
Structural necessity vs symbolic representation of earth plane
Variations in height and accessibility across different stupas
Presence of second vedika on medhi level

concepts.name: Stupa Chronology: Mauryan to Gupta Period
key_dimensions: Ashokan stupas (3rd century BCE): Sanchi I core, brick construction
Sunga enlargements (2nd-1st century BCE): stone casing, torana additions
Satavahana contributions (1st-2nd century CE): Amaravati, narrative panels
Gupta refinements (4th-5th century CE): Sarnath, Nalanda modifications

concepts.name: Regional Stupa Variations: Mainland vs Periphery
key_dimensions: Gandhara stupas: tall cylindrical drums, Greek-influenced decoration
Deccan stupas (Amaravati): elongated anda, elaborate ayaka platforms
Sri Lankan stupas (dagobas): massive scale, bell-shaped domes
Southeast Asian adaptations: Borobudur (mandala plan), Shwedagon (bell-shaped)

concepts.name: Relic Deposition and Consecration Practices
key_dimensions: Types of relics: sarira (bodily), paribhogika (used objects), uddesika (commemorative)
Relic caskets: nested containers, inscriptions, precious materials
Placement within anda: central chamber vs harmika
Archaeological evidence: Piprahwa, Bhattiprolu relic discoveries

concepts.name: Aniconic vs Iconic Representation in Stupa Art
key_dimensions: Early phase (pre-1st century CE): symbols only (wheel, tree, footprints, throne)
Transitional phase: Gandhara and Mathura anthropomorphic Buddha emergence
Reasons for aniconism: philosophical (Buddha beyond form) vs artistic convention
Jataka narratives without Buddha images vs later iconic versions

concepts.name: Sanchi Stupa Complex: Architectural Layers
key_dimensions: Stupa I (Great Stupa): Mauryan core, Sunga enlargement, Satavahana toranas
Stupa II: unique position (hillside), continuous narrative friezes
Stupa III: single torana, relics of Sariputta and Moggallana
Monastic establishments (viharas) and their relationship to stupas

concepts.name: Amaravati School: Distinctive Features
key_dimensions: Ayaka platforms and pillars: five projections with narrative panels
Marble/limestone vs sandstone: material distinction from North India
Dynamic sculptural style: movement, emotion, narrative complexity
Influence on Southeast Asian art (Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Thailand)

concepts.name: Stupa Iconography: Jataka and Buddha Life Scenes
key_dimensions: Jataka tales: Vessantara, Mahakapi, Chaddanta on Sanchi toranas
Buddha's life events: Birth, Enlightenment, First Sermon, Mahaparinirvana
Directional associations: specific events on specific torana faces
Narrative techniques: continuous narration, episodic panels, symbolic condensation

concepts.name: Stupa vs Chaitya: Architectural Distinctions
key_dimensions: Stupa: freestanding monument vs Chaitya: rock-cut prayer hall with stupa
Structural independence vs integrated architecture
Open-air worship vs enclosed congregational space
Examples: Sanchi (stupa) vs Karla, Bhaja (chaityas)

concepts.name: Votive Stupas and Miniature Traditions
key_dimensions: Small stupas surrounding main stupa: Sanchi, Nalanda examples
Individual donations and inscriptions
Terracotta and metal miniature stupas: portable worship objects
Distinction from main relic stupas in purpose and scale

concepts.name: Stupa Construction Materials and Techniques
key_dimensions: Early phase: brick core with wooden railings (Mauryan)
Stone casing and replication of wooden forms (Sunga-Satavahana)
Regional material preferences: sandstone (North), limestone (Deccan)
Structural engineering: load distribution, weathering considerations

concepts.name: Pradakshina (Circumambulation): Ritual and Architecture
key_dimensions: Clockwise movement: symbolic significance (following sun's path)
Two-level circumambulation: ground and medhi levels
Architectural facilitation: vedika spacing, entrance alignments
Narrative sequence on railings guiding devotee movement

concepts.name: UNESCO World Heritage Stupas: Conservation Issues
key_dimensions: Sanchi (1989): preservation challenges, tourism management
Comparison with other Buddhist sites: Ajanta, Ellora inclusion criteria
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) conservation methods
Modern threats: weathering, vandalism, inappropriate restoration

concepts.name: Stupa Symbolism: Cosmological Interpretations
key_dimensions: Five elements representation: earth (base), water (anda), fire (harmika), air (chattra), ether (yasti)
Mandala concept: cosmic diagram in three dimensions
Mount Meru symbolism: cosmic mountain at center of universe
Buddhist philosophical concepts: impermanence, nirvana embodied in architecture
